purpose: Independent source and semantic expectations for current-pipeline DAP migration; not a runtime test result or a new runtime interface.
stop_convention: Each DAP_STOP marks an executable source line. Expected locals are immediately before that statement. Resolve markers from source instead of hard-coding line numbers.
output_convention: Expected stdout is decoded payload bytes, independent of the number of DAP output events; embedded NUL must survive framing.

checks: Break on inner_update and inspect both frames with distinct value locals.
At outer_call, stepIn reaches inner; next crosses inner without stopping inside it; stepOut from inner resumes outer_return. Use separate fresh sessions.
At inner_update, evaluate doubled + 2 returns 42, leaves doubled at 40, and normal output remains 44.
At inner_update, set mutable doubled to 99; the following update makes it 100 and final stdout is 103\n. A fresh session without setVariable remains 44\n.
Reject unknown names, stale frames and invalid variable references without changing state or locals.
Display only published mixed-runtime boundaries; preserve the same result for VM-to-native-to-VM and native-to-VM-to-native. No arbitrary native source-step promise.
Expand the current array and snapshot independently; inspection must not mutate either.
A retained inspect result has an explicit lifetime; release all owned copies and reference handles on resume, cancellation and disconnect.
An old variablesReference cannot resolve to an unrelated object after resume or restart.
Reject writes to immutable snapshot/title; type-incompatible mutable writes leave the old value intact.
Cancel while paused and prove physical allocator baseline after final owner and code-lease release.
Condition index == 2 stops once with sum 1.
Hit condition 3 stops on the third encounter with index 2 and sum 1.
Logpoint index={index},sum={sum} produces the four fixed pairs without stopped events.
Replacing the file breakpoint set removes previous conditions and hit counters.
Pause/continue/cancel must use a bounded execution fixture from the published hook tests; do not make this short loop a timing race.
With caught exceptions enabled, stop at the throw and expose the exception before continuing to the handler.
With only uncaught enabled, this handled language error does not stop at throw.
Exception value remains owned until inspection completes; cancellation and formatting OOM release it.
Preserve language error versus panic, cancellation, resource and host-service distinctions; the latter are not caught language exceptions.
With uncaught enabled, expose DapFailure.Expected; after continue report unsuccessful execution and exactly one session termination.
Never print unreachable; preserve exception ownership and final physical baseline.
Compare error category and source span, not an invented numeric exit code or provider-specific formatting.

completion_caveat: These source fixtures have passed fresh reference syntax/check/ordinary execution against the published development baseline. DAP breakpoints, stepping, inspection, mutation, mixed callbacks, resource/FI and sanitizer qualification of the full consumer remain required. They are not yet registered as DAP end-to-end gates.
